entities.name: PMID:10727665
observations: Primary study titled “Methylation of the estrogen receptor-alpha gene promoter is selectively increased in proliferating human aortic smooth muscle cells” (Cardiovascular Research, 2000).
Compared normal in situ human aortic smooth muscle cells with explanted, cultured proliferating cells.

entities.name: ESR1
observations: The estrogen receptor-alpha promoter appeared unmethylated in normal aortic tissue but methylated in proliferating cultured human aortic smooth muscle cells.
Southern blot, COBRA, and RLGS-M assays assessed methylation; RLGS-M supported a selective locus-level change rather than generalized methylation.

entities.name: Human aortic smooth muscle cells
observations: Normal in situ cells had a contractile phenotype, whereas explanted cultured cells were dedifferentiated and proliferative.
The study supports selectivity among methylated loci within this cell system, but did not establish specificity relative to other cell types.

entities.name: ESR1 promoter methylation
observations: ESR1 promoter methylation was selectively increased when human aortic smooth muscle cells changed from normal in situ to proliferating cultured cells.
The evidence supports locus-level selectivity, not cell-type specificity; the primary report was available at abstract level.
